intentAndPurpose.intent: Binary selection control for forms and settings with tri-state (indeterminate) support.

forbids: use as a toggle for non-boolean values

rules.name: readOnly
useWhen: display-only state, value visible but not editable

props.name: accent
props.description: accent property

props.name: appearance
props.description: Appearance role — border, hover, and checked fill. `auto` → secondary stack.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: For composite fields — links to `Field.Description` etc.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Invalid state for form validation (exposed on the checkbox control).

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label when there is no visible `label` (or when overriding the visible copy). Maps directly to `aria-label` on the underlying checkbox control. When using `CheckboxField`, the visible `Field.Label` provides association automatically — prefer that over `aria-label`.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the checkbox is checked (controlled)

props.name: children
props.description: children property

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test automation id — forwarded to the checkbox control (`BaseCheckbox.Root`).

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Default checked state (uncontrolled)

props.name: description
props.description: Supplementary copy below the label row. Maps to `aria-describedby` on the control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the checkbox is disabled

props.name: errorHighlight
props.description: Error-state chrome on the wrapper (from `CheckboxField` when invalid). Standalone `Checkbox` does not use `errorHighlight`; use `CheckboxField` for validation UX.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Whether the checkbox is in indeterminate state

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label beside the control. Maps to `aria-label` when the wrapper is a `div`.

props.name: labelWrapper
props.description: Outer wrapper element. Use `'div'` inside `CheckboxField` (with `Field.Label`) so the visible label is not nested inside a second `<label>`.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name for form submission

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Change handler

props.name: parent
props.description: Marks this checkbox as the select-all parent of its `CheckboxGroup`. Base UI then DERIVES `checked` / `indeterminate` from the children — do not pass either prop yourself — and toggling it selects or clears the whole group. Requires `allValues` on the surrounding `<CheckboxGroup>`.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the checkbox is read-only (visually distinct from disabled)

props.name: required
props.description: HTML required — form validation when unchecked

props.name: size
props.description: Size preset. Default: 'm'

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles

props.name: value
props.description: Value used when inside a CheckboxGroup

interactionBehavior.summary: Checkbox scales UP on press (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`, 7%), the opposite of Button's squash. Two claims usually surprise people. First, `Enter` does NOT toggle it — Base UI deliberately cancels the native button activation and forwards `Enter` to the form's default submitter, so only `Space` (on key-up) checks the box. Second, its focus ring is not `--Focus-Outline`: the outer ring is `--Informative-Bold`, per the Figma spec — the same selection-control pattern Radio, Switch and the slider knob share. The `appearance` prop colours the CHECKED fill only; the unchecked stroke and the unchecked hover/press tints come from the nearest `<Surface>` role, falling back to Neutral on a bare page.
hover: Both hover rules are wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck tint behind.

UNCHECKED hover fills the box interior with `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Hover` (Neutral by default) while the border stays at the unchecked stroke — so the box tints without committing to the brand colour.
CHECKED or INDETERMINATE hover steps both `background-color` and `border-color` to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`, following the `appearance` prop.

The unchecked hover role is resolved at render time into `data-unchecked-appearance`: no `<Surface>` ancestor, or a Surface sitting at a palette extreme (step 100 or 2500), resolves to Neutral; any in-between step — including dark `default` around step 200 — inherits the Surface's role.
There is no hover styling on the label or description text, and no hover rule on the wrapper — only the box reacts.
press: The box scales UP: `transform: scale(calc(1 + var(--_tap-scale) / 100))` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` at 7%. Button scales DOWN — Checkbox, Radio, and IconButton go the other way.
UNCHECKED press tints the interior to `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Pressed`; CHECKED / INDETERMINATE press moves fill and border to `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed`.
Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a finger tap gets the same tint and the same scale-up a mouse press does.
focus: The halo is the standard two-layer shape — an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` — but the OUTER ring is `--Informative-Bold` (falling back to `--Focus-Outline`), not the brand focus colour. Checkbox's focus ring therefore stays informative-blue even on a `negative` or `positive` checkbox.
`:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible indicator is `:focus-visible`, so clicking the label does not paint a ring.

The halo follows the box's own radius, which is per size (`--Shape-1` at `s`, `--Shape-1-5` at `m`, `--Shape-2` at `l`, all overridable via `--Checkbox-borderRadius`), and it is a `box-shadow` on the box only — the label and description are never ringed.
A `readOnly` checkbox is still focusable and nothing suppresses its `:focus-visible` rule, so it still shows the halo even though hover and press are dead.
keyboard: `Space` toggles, and it fires on key-up — Base UI renders a `<span role="checkbox">` (not a native button) alongside a hidden native input, so activation follows `role="button"` key-up semantics.

`Enter` does NOT toggle. Base UI intercepts `Enter` on `keydown`, cancels the native activation, and instead clicks the enclosing form's default submit button — so `Enter` on a focused checkbox submits the form.
The default wrapper is a real `<label>` element around the control, so the label text and the description are part of the same hit target and clicking them toggles the box.

Passing `labelWrapper="div"` or `labelAssociation="field"` (what `CheckboxField` does) swaps the wrapper to a `<div>`, which deliberately breaks that implicit label association — the outer `Field.Label` provides it instead, and an `aria-label` is derived from `label` / `description`.
`disabled` sets the native disabled attribute plus `aria-disabled`, removing the control from the tab order; `readOnly` sets `aria-readonly` and keeps it in the tab order.
selected: Checked and indeterminate share the same fill: `background-color` and `border-color` both go to `--{Role}-Bold`, with the glyph in `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y`. `appearance="auto"` (the default) resolves to the `secondary` role for the whole stack.

The tick bursts inward rather than fading in: the indicator rests at `scale(--_cb-burst-scale)` — the box/icon ratio for that size, 1.333 at `s`, 1.25 at `m`, 1.333 at `l` — and animates to `scale(1)` on check, so at the start of the animation the glyph exactly fills the box with no clipping.
These transitions do not fire on mount (no value change), so a page of unchecked checkboxes loads silently with no flash of animating ticks.

The check and minus glyphs are BOTH always in the DOM, stacked absolutely. Unchecked parks both at `rotate(0deg)`/`opacity: 0` so the unchecked→checked and unchecked→indeterminate paths show no phantom rotation.
Checked ↔ indeterminate is the only path where rotation is visible: the tick rotates 0° → 45° while the minus rotates -45° → 0°, in lockstep.
Indeterminate is a controlled prop, not a third click state — a click dispatches on the hidden native input, so it always resolves to checked or unchecked.
disabled: `disabled` dims the whole row — the wrapper carries `opacity: var(--Disabled-Opacity)`, so the label and description dim with the box — and sets `cursor: not-allowed` on the wrapper.

Here the `not-allowed` cursor IS observable, unlike on Button and Chip: the box takes `pointer-events: none`, so the label wrapper becomes the hit target and its own `cursor: not-allowed` is what the pointer shows.

`readOnly` is styled as a deliberately different state, not a dimmer one: no opacity reduction at all (`.wrapper[data-disabled]:not([data-readonly])` owns the dim), `cursor: default`, and `pointer-events: none` on the box.

A `readOnly` checked box fills with `--{Role}-High` instead of the brand `--{Role}-Bold`, and its glyph is recoloured to `--Surface-Halo-Gap` (the current surface colour) so it cannot flip light-on-light in dark mode. A `readOnly` unchecked box gets a `--{Role}-High` border, and its unchecked role is forced to Neutral.

`readOnly` is guarded in three places: `onCheckedChange` is not wired up, `pointer-events: none` on the box blocks pointer input, and `readOnly` is forwarded to `BaseCheckbox.Root` so Base UI's own guard returns early from both its click handler and the hidden input's `change`. Keyboard `Space` therefore cannot change the value either, controlled or uncontrolled. Base UI also emits `aria-readonly` itself, matching what the wrapper already sets.
touch: Hover tints never apply on touch-only devices; the pressed tint plus the 7% scale-up are the entire response to a tap.
Growing on press is the right direction for a control this small — the box expands out from under the fingertip that is covering it.
Because the default wrapper is a `<label>`, the label and description text extend the touch target well beyond the 16/20/24px box; the control↔label gap stays a flat `--Spacing-1-5` at every size.
